title: The Halloween battle with Duke Ellington in Kansas City
summary: Clayton says the raggedy Basie band was outclassed by Duke Ellington's in 1936.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving

blocks.x: Did you ever play a battle with Duke anywhere?
What, that night during your relief?
Yes. The night we were, Halloween night.
That's the only time you had, I mean, the time you played?
We were a little raggedy band trying to play against Duke Ellington. We felt we,
we felt like, I guess we felt like Lionel Hampton's band did.
Yes, after you got through with it?

I don't know why because Duke had so much. He had everything, but you listen to some of the guys, 'we can match them, we can out-swing them cats.' Although we just played little old stuff we had which wasn't very much. I, to me now, it wasn't even a battle considering who, all the guys that Duke had, and everything that they were doing in '36. It couldn't have been much of a battle.
Funny, that was a very, well sort of integrated band at that time. You know, everything was balanced wasn't it?
It was the greatest, yes. It was a beautiful band.
But of course, it depends to some extent on what program, I mean, he elects to play. You know, it's not necessarily going to pull out the swinging things. (LAUGHTER).
